cases.title: Deep Learning Research Engineer
cases.description:
HackerRank helps companies like NVIDIA, Amazon, and Microsoft hire and upskill the next generation of developers based on skills, not pedigree. Our platform is trusted by over 2,500 of the world’s most innovative companies to build strong engineering teams ready for what’s next.
Software has entered an era where humans and AI build side by side. As this shift accelerates, the definition of strong technical talent is changing. We give companies better ways to identify and invest in next-generation skills.
People at HackerRank care deeply about the impact of their work and sweat the small details so our customers can be wildly successful with products they genuinely love to use. We move with urgency and believe great outcomes come from high standards.

Hiring is one of the most consequential decisions a company makes. 3,000+ enterprises rely on HackerRank to get it right. We are now reinventing how that works for the agentic era. The AI/ML systems that power this platform are not auxiliary features. They are the product.
Open Problems
The agentic era is reshaping every layer of the hiring stack. These are some of the core problems you'll be working across, none of them fully solved.
- Chakra: Building an autonomous AI interviewer that conducts, adapts to, and evaluates technical interviews end to end.
- Integrity: Detecting fraud and suspicious behavior across multiple signal types. The ways candidates game assessments change frequently, and the models need to keep up.
- Evaluation: Measuring technical skill in a world where AI writes the code. The old proxies no longer hold and the new ones have not been defined yet.
Your focus will shift across these depending on where the highest-leverage work is at any given time.
What you will do
- Research, Design, and Develop advanced Deep Learning models and novel Neural architectures.
- Explore architectures beyond Transformers, including State Space Models (SSMs), Liquid Neural Networks (LNNs), and Hybrid approaches.
- Design and implement Agentic AI systems, Recursive Reasoning Engines, and tool-augmented architectures.
- Fine-tuning of models using PEFT (e.g. LoRA, QLoRA etc.), and Knowledge Distillation.
- Optimize model Performance, Inference Efficiency, Latency, and Memory utilization.
- Design rigorous experiments, evaluation frameworks, and benchmarks to validate research hypotheses.
- Translate cutting-edge research into scalable, production-grade AI systems.
Who you are
- M.Tech./M.S./Ph.D. in AI/ML or related disciplines, preferably from a Tier 1 premier Research Institution.
- 2–3 years of experience in Deep Learning, Machine Learning, or Applied AI Research.
- Strong foundations in Linear Algebra, Probability, Statistics, Optimization, and Deep Learning algorithms.
- Proficient in frameworks like PyTorch/JAX, with hands-on model development experience.
- Demonstrated ability to implement, reproduce, and extend research papers, including building neural architectures from scratch.
- Familiarity with distributed computing, GPU acceleration, and scalable ML infrastructure.
- Strong understanding of experimental design, model evaluation, benchmarking, and statistical validation.
- Demonstrated research aptitude through publications, open-source contributions etc.
Even better if you have
- Publications at top venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL) or notable open-source contributions in model architectures or agentic systems.
- Experience with LLM evaluation, fraud or anomaly detection, or building systems where the “ground truth” is still being defined.
- Hands-on work taking models from research into low-latency, production inference, such as quantization, distillation, or serving optimization.
You will thrive here if you
- You enjoy solving open-ended research problems and challenging established assumptions.
- You prefer first-principles thinking and rigorous experimentation over simply applying existing models.
- You are excited to explore next-generation AI architectures beyond traditional Transformers.
- You thrive in a fast-paced environment with intellectual freedom, ownership, and direct collaboration with leadership.
- You are passionate about turning novel AI research into efficient, scalable, real-world systems.

Intermediate Backend Engineer, Security Factory: Code Security
An overview of this role
As an Intermediate Backend Engineer on GitLab's Security Factory: Code Security team, you'll help developers find and fix security issues in the code they write and the open source components they depend on.
Your work connects dependency analysis, vulnerability detection, and automated remediation. You'll build parsing that tells the security analysis engine which libraries and frameworks a project uses, extend a service that turns security advisories into dependency update merge requests, and develop hybrid analyzers that combine rule-based detection with artificial intelligence (AI) reasoning. You'll help evaluate how well those analyzers find real vulnerabilities and expand coverage of libraries, frameworks, and AI agent tooling.
We use AI-assisted development tools in our daily work and expect you to use them effectively and with good judgment.
What you’ll do
- Develop secure, well-tested, performant parsing for dependency manifests, lockfiles, and software bills of materials (SBOMs). Extend support for new package ecosystems and formats in the analysis engine and remediation service.
- Build and apply analyzers that combine deterministic analysis with AI-driven analysis, working with the team's technical leadership. Review their results and measure false positives and missed findings against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities.
- Create detection rules mapped to Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) and the test fixtures that prove they work.
- Contribute to packaging analyzers for continuous integration (CI) jobs, AI agent workflows, and command-line tools, reporting findings in GitLab's standard security report formats.
- Extend the automated remediation service, from running dependency updates in a sandbox to opening merge requests.
- Solve technical problems of moderate scope and complexity. Identify technical debt that slows the team down, and propose and implement improvements.
- Write maintainable code that meets our internal standards, and help maintain those standards through code review.
- Participate in on-call rotations to troubleshoot product operations, security operations, and urgent engineering issues.
What you’ll bring
- Experience using AI or large language model (LLM) tools to generate or evaluate technical content, with the judgment to know when output is trustworthy and when it isn't.
- Solid professional experience writing and testing production code in a systems language, particularly Go and/or Rust. We use both, plus Ruby for remediation and Python for some analyzers, and value a willingness to work across them.
- A willingness to learn how vulnerabilities arise in code and the software supply chain, explore common vulnerability classes such as the Open Worldwide Application Security Project (OWASP) Top 10 and CWE, and apply static analysis to detect them. Deep expertise isn't required, and we'll help you develop it.
- The ability to organize your work and follow through on tasks independently in a remote, largely asynchronous environment.
- The ability to communicate clearly and concisely about technical problems and propose iterative solutions.
- Helpful, but not required: experience with containerized workflows and continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), or a willingness to learn them; package managers and dependency tooling such as npm, Maven, pip, Bundler, or Cargo; web or mobile frameworks; parsing, abstract syntax trees (ASTs), program analysis, or detection rules; or evaluating AI-driven detection against labeled data. We use Docker heavily.
About the team
The Security Factory: Code Security team builds GitLab's code-level security scanning capabilities, spanning static application security testing (SAST) and dependency scanning.
We work closely with the Static Analysis team on GitLab's SAST engines, with Composition Analysis on the broader software supply chain, and with other groups across the Sec section. We rely heavily on asynchronous work across time zones.

The Elastic IT team is shifting beyond standard chat interfaces to craft the next frontier of generative and agentic AI experiences. We are looking for an innovative UX & Front End Engineer to join our team to bridge the gap between powerful AI capabilities and intuitive, delightful user interfaces that accelerate productivity across the entire organization.
Our ideal candidate is a skilled front-end engineer with hands-on experience designing and building AI user experiences (e.g., streaming text, dynamic prompt workflows, agent reasoning visualizations, and multi-modal interaction patterns). In this role, you will leverage the latest AI technologies and the Elastic Stack (including ESRE, Agent Builder, Workflows and eUI) to build high-performance front-end applications for a suite of internal products and platforms. Driven by a user-centered mindset, you will act as a key collaborator between AI back-end engineers, product managers, and user groups to turn complex AI reasoning into seamless human-AI interactions. By shaping how enterprise users interact with generative AI, you will enable our global workforce while showcasing the boundary-pushing capabilities of Elastic's products.
Are you ready to design and build the interfaces that supercharge enterprise productivity and prove what’s possible with Elastic? Join us to create AI user experiences that turn collective knowledge into instant action, empowering everyone at Elastic to achieve more.

cases.description:
Software Engineer, Business Systems
Function: Business Technology & Security — Business Systems
Location: Pune, India · Hybrid
Reports to: Product Manager, Business Systems
Experience: 2–4 years
Short description
Build and run the integrations, pipelines, automations and internal tools that connect Mindtickle's business systems — Salesforce, NetSuite, HRMS, Slack and Google Cloud. You take defined requirements and own the technical path end to end: design, build, ship, and keep it running.
About the team
Business Technology & Security runs the systems, automation and security behind how Mindtickle operates. Business Systems is its build engine — the team that turns requirements from GTM, Finance, People Success, IT, Legal and Security into shipped systems: integrations, data pipelines, automations, internal tools and agents.
We are a small team. You will not be part of a traditional engineering squad with sprints and Scrum ceremonies. You will operate independently, usually owning a problem from a defined requirement through to a deployed, monitored solution — and then continuing to own it.
The role
You are the engineer on the team. When a system needs to talk to another system, when a manual process needs to become an automated one, when a tool needs to exist and doesn't — you build it.
Requirements come to you defined. The Product Manager and Business Systems Analyst own the business problem, the stakeholders, and the question of whether we should do it at all. The technical path is entirely yours — how it's designed, what it's built on, how it's tested, how it fails safely, and how it's supported once it's live.
What you'll own
Building — about half your time Integrations between business systems. Data pipelines. Automations that remove manual work from Finance, People Success, IT, Security and GTM. Internal tools and lightweight services. AI-backed workflows and agents where they are the right answer, and conventional code where they are not.
Running it — about a fifth of your time You inherit a set of automations already in production and become their owner. Monitoring, alerting, incident response, and the unglamorous work of making inherited systems observable and documented. Nothing you build gets handed to someone else to support.
Technical evaluation — about 15% When the team is deciding whether to build or buy, or whether a vendor's API can actually do what the demo claimed, you build the prototype that answers it. Deep technical spikes, integration feasibility, and performance and security reality-checks — against a requirement the Product Manager and Analyst have already defined.
Migrations — about 15% Data migration, field mapping, cutover scripts and system replacements as we move platforms.
The shape of a typical week
Daily — Writing Python with Claude Code. Reading vendor API documentation. Wiring REST and GraphQL APIs, webhooks and event-driven flows. Debugging a sync that silently dropped records. Deploying to Cloud Run.
Weekly — Shipping an increment and demoing it. Working through requirements with the Product Manager and Analyst. Triaging what broke.
Monthly — One meaningful capability live in production, with monitoring, a runbook, and documentation good enough that someone else could pick it up.
Stack
Python · Google Apps Script · Google Cloud Platform (Cloud Run, Cloud Functions, Cloud Scheduler, Pub/Sub, BigQuery, Firestore, Cloud Storage, Compute Engine) · REST and GraphQL APIs, webhooks, OAuth and service-account authentication · Claude Code and modern AI tooling as a primary way of working · Git and CI/CD
Business systems you will integrate with: Salesforce, NetSuite, HRMS, Slack, Google Workspace, and the wider SaaS estate.
What we're looking for
We care about what you have built and kept alive, not the tools listed on your CV.
2–4 years building software, integrations or automations in a professional environment
Strong Python, and real fluency with APIs — authentication, rate limits, retries, idempotency, pagination, webhooks and event-driven patterns
You have built integrations against SaaS APIs, not only configured them through consoles or drag-and-drop integration platforms
Hands-on cloud experience (GCP preferred; AWS or Azure is fine) with a working understanding of how to compose services rather than follow a tutorial
End-to-end ownership you can point to — a system you designed, built, shipped and then operated. Something that broke in production and you fixed it.
Debugging across system boundaries — when two systems disagree about the same record, you can work out why
Testing and verification instinct — you know your output is correct because you measured it, not because it ran without erroring
Fast on unfamiliar ground — you have picked up a stack you didn't know and shipped it. This matters more to us than prior exposure to any specific technology.
Clear written communication — design notes, runbooks, and documentation are part of the job, not an afterthought
Nice to have
Building AI agents, tool-use, and agentic workflows; MCP servers
Exposure to business systems — CRM, ERP, HRIS, ITSM — and the SaaS ecosystem around them
Data and pipeline work (BigQuery, ETL/ELT)
